text: The Great Wall of China is not visible to the naked eye from the Moon, according to NASA astronauts and multiple space agencies; this has been confirmed by direct observation reports.
The Great Wall is only about 9 meters wide on average, far too narrow to be resolved by the human eye from orbital distances, let alone from the Moon.
Astronaut Chris Hadfield has stated that many human-made structures, including highways, are visible from low Earth orbit, but this is very different from being visible from the Moon.

Humans typically use only about 10% of their brain at any given time is a myth; brain imaging studies show that nearly all regions of the brain have a function and are used, just not all simultaneously.
The '10 percent of the brain' myth likely originated from a misinterpretation of neuroscience findings in the early 20th century and has been repeatedly debunked by neurologists.
Functional MRI studies show that even simple tasks activate large, distributed networks across the brain, not just a small fraction of it.
Goldfish have a memory span of at least several months, not three seconds, according to peer-reviewed studies on fish cognition and behavior.
Researchers have trained goldfish to respond to specific cues and retain the learned behavior for weeks, contradicting the popular three-second memory claim.
Vaccines undergo multiple phases of clinical trials before approval, and large-scale post-market surveillance systems continue to monitor for rare adverse effects.
Peer-reviewed meta-analyses involving millions of participants have found no causal link between standard childhood vaccines and autism spectrum disorder.
The original 1998 study claiming a vaccine-autism link was retracted by The Lancet due to data manipulation and ethical violations by the lead author.
The Great Barrier Reef has experienced significant coral bleaching events in 2016, 2017, and 2020, primarily linked to rising sea temperatures.
Some sections of the Great Barrier Reef have shown partial recovery in coral cover between major bleaching events, according to long-term monitoring programs.
Scientists agree that repeated bleaching events reduce the reef's ability to fully recover, even when short-term recovery is observed in specific regions.
Lightning can and does strike the same place multiple times; tall structures like the Empire State Building are struck by lightning dozens of times per year.
Lightning rods are specifically designed on the principle that lightning preferentially strikes the same tall, conductive points repeatedly.
